## The gap: timely, rigorous, and collaborative evidence

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
- Chris Whitty, then Chief Scientific Adviser and later Chief Medical
  Officer for England, outlined what was needed of modelling evidence to
  inform policy effectively
- Current approaches struggle to be timely, rigorous, and collaborative
  all at once
- Multi-model efforts combine forecasts from several teams and rarely
  collaborate on model components
- Common components would let a difference in results be attributed to
  an assumption rather than an implementation

::: {.attribution}
Whitty (2015),
[doi:10.1186/s12916-015-0544-8](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12916-015-0544-8) ·
